HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. KOREAN FACES on everyone in frame: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, blue, grey or green, never the whole eyeball painted solid black); a low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European nose. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. GRAND EXPOSITION of the last siege. LAND SIEGE — no ships, no sea, no oars. Crane / slight aerial, FAR WIDE. ONE DEVICE: Pyongyang fortress as the attached board — grey stone ridge, red two-tier munru, Taedong river a silver band at the left, packed-earth roads. Three Tang columns as tiny painted masses closing the ring from the north-west road (from the Amnok), camp-smoke, vermilion banners on poles. Goguryeo red three-legged-crow banners ONLY on the wall. LEFT of the sheet = Xue Rengui a SMALL white-coated figure in the lower third on a pale horse, cream lamellar, red sash, fangtian ji, NEVER a ring sword. Storm sky, one cloud-break shaft on the red pavilion. Fire not yet on the towers. Armies at true human size, dissolving in haze. BANNERS BY SIDE: vermilion Tang ONLY in the camps; red crow ONLY on the wall; Tang cloth plain, no readable character. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. BATTLE ACTION FRAME in the same painted look, NOT a calm posed still: a real battle caught mid-moment, like a frame from a big-budget animated war film. The camera is INSIDE the fight — low over the water among the oars, on a heaving deck, or at a hard dutch angle — with a dark out-of-focus foreground shape close to the lens (a gunwale, an oar blade, a shield rim, a banner, a burning spar). LOTS OF FIRE: sails and decks burning in painted flame with heat shimmer, columns of black and orange smoke, sparks and embers driving across the frame, firelight on wet faces and steel. ARMIES: dozens to hundreds of soldiers in frame at true human size against the ships — packed along gunwales, climbing, falling, rowing, loosing arrows — the nearest fully drawn and acting, the far ones massed painted shapes in the smoke. MOTION: spray thrown off oars and bows, arrows streaking in long lines, cloth, hair and banners whipping, bodies mid-leap and mid-fall, motion blur on the fastest things. EMOTION: every near face acts — screaming orders, terror, rage, grief, gritted teeth, soot and spray on the skin. WATER is a real painted sea — heavy dark swells, foam, fire reflected in it — never Hokusai claw waves, never woodblock or scroll stylisation, never flat cartoon shapes, never toy boats. The same ships, banners and shoreline in every frame of this battle. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = xuerengui. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_pyongyang_fortress (keep this exact architecture and ground). KOREAN FACES on every person, named or extra: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a small catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, honey, gold, blue, grey, green or purple). Never paint the entire eyeball solid black. A low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European, Roman or Persian nose. East Asian bone: single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair. Never Western, Latin, or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes. XUE RENGUI Colour #e8e3d5. PLACE pyongyang_fortress — attached board /pl_pyongyang_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Pyongyang fortress: the same red two-tier munru on the stone ridge in every still. Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Tang banners: vermilion silk with a yellow sun disc and a dark brush glyph inside it — painted as an illegible brush mark, never readable text. Attached flag /flag_tang.png. Goguryeo banners: red silk with the black three-legged crow inside a studded black sun-ring. Attached flag /flag_goguryeo.png. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
